articles.title: This Might Be The Most Passive-Aggressive Thing You Can Text Someone
articles.summary: This widely recognized gesture is also one of the most misunderstood.
articles.body:
If you want to annoy your friends and co-workers, reply to their message with one of the most widely recognized gestures: a thumbs-up emoji.

The affirmative gesture that was originally meant to signal "OK" in certain cultures can mean anything but in digital communication. This reaction may be perceived as passive-aggressive, disinterested or sarcastic in a text, depending on how it's used in an online conversation.

When singer Kelly Clarkson called out a New York City store that did not sell her an animatronic bird she wanted, she wrote on social media. "Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," and added a thumbs-up emoji. In that case, the thumbs-up emoji did not suggest agreement with its intended recipient and that all was well.

Or consider the "IsThisUnprofessional" subreddit, where a confused co-worker declared that he thought the reaction meant "Got it, no notes, we're good," but his younger co-worker later told him his "bare thumbs up reads as cold, like the texting version of an eye roll."

"Now I'm sitting here wondering if I've been low-key insulting people for years and nobody bothered to tell me," the befuddled 35-year-old continued in his post.

One reason for this ongoing confusion may be generational differences between people who see a thumbs-up emoji as passive-aggressive and those who see it as an innocuous "liking" reaction built into platforms like Facebook and Instagram. One 2025 survey found that nearly 4 in 10 workers –– 38% –– use the "thumbs up" reaction to signal agreement, but a growing number of younger colleagues say it can feel dismissive or sarcastic.

"The thumbs up replaces a range of different ways we can respond in face-to-face conversation," linguist Lauren Gawne, who ran research for that survey, told HuffPost. "You can nod or say something or just start doing something, but this all gets flattened into a single option that people bring their own meaning to."

Etiquette problems often arise "when something's unclear or when we assume something," said Nick Leighton, an etiquette expert and host of the "Were You Raised by Wolves?" podcast. "The thumbs-up emoji is a great example: It has different meanings to different people. And once we lack crystal clarity, this is where the trouble starts."

"In a work setting, where efficiency is prized, a 'thumbs up' is likely just an acknowledgment," Leighton said as an example. "But if your boss is known to be passive-aggressive in general, then your mileage may vary."

Why The Thumbs-Up Emoji Can Feel So Hostile In A Text

Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost .

What makes the thumbs-up reaction even more ambiguous is when it's presented without any more reassuring context. In a text, a one-word "OK" reply can feel hostile, because brief answers imply a lack of effort, linguistics experts say . This is also why answering only "sure" to your friend's request for your time can make them feel unsure if you actually want to attend their party.

"This is especially true when the thumbs-up isn't proportional to the message you're responding to," Leighton said. "If I just sent you a long heartfelt paragraph about my feelings, you're going to have to do better than just give me a thumbs-up."

Similarly, this is why using the "thumbs-up" tap-back emoji reaction that Apple provides iPhone users can create headaches. When your friend only provides a reaction that takes just a tap to share, it may also imply they barely read your message.

You can certainly lose your mind dissecting whether your colleague's emoji reaction or your grandparent's thumbs-up reaction was a personal attack, or you can assume the best intentions. Instead of agonizing over the meaning of your friend or boss's thumbs-up emoji, try Leighton's Zen approach:

"Rare is the person who's genuinely going out of their way to be rude," he said. "In the end, they're just little pictures and it's best to [not] read too much into them."

articles.title: Microplásticos no sangue de animais são achados até no Pantanal | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo encontrou partículas em 43 de 47 antas e tamanduás-bandeira analisados no Brasil. Animais mais próximos de áreas modificadas pelo homem tinham concentrações maiores.
articles.summary: Estudo encontrou partículas em 43 de 47 antas e tamanduás-bandeira analisados no Brasil. Animais mais próximos de áreas modificadas pelo homem tinham concentrações maiores.
articles.body:
Tamanduá-bandeira atravessa estrada em Mato Grosso do Sul. — Foto: Luiz Felipe Mendes

Microplásticos foram encontrados no sangue de antas e tamanduás-bandeira que vivem em diferentes regiões do Brasil, inclusive em áreas remotas do Pantanal, aponta um novo estudo publicado na revista científica "Nature" nesta quarta-feira (11).

Os pesquisadores analisaram amostras de sangue de 26 antas e 21 tamanduás-bandeira , coletadas na Amazônia, no Cerrado e no Pantanal entre 2021 e 2022. As partículas apareceram em 43 dos 47 animais.

Ainda segundo o estudo, a concentração média foi de 73,8 partículas por mililitro de sangue , mas os valores variaram bastante entre os indivíduos .

As antas apresentaram, em média, concentrações maiores que os tamanduás, embora a diferença entre as espécies não tenha sido considerada estatisticamente significativa.

📝 ENTENDA : Os microplásticos são partículas de plástico menores que 5 milímetros. Por serem muito pequenos, podem se espalhar pelo ambiente pelo ar, pela chuva, por rios, pela água subterrânea e por enchentes.

O estudo combinou as análises do sangue com dados de GPS que mostravam por onde cada animal circulava.

A partir disso, os pesquisadores encontraram um padrão: quanto maior a presença de atividades humanas no território ocupado pelos animais, maior tendia a ser a quantidade de microplásticos no sangue.

Também foram registradas concentrações maiores entre animais que viviam mais perto de áreas construídas e de instalações de tratamento ou armazenamento de resíduos.

“Isso nos permitiu ver que quanto maior a intervenção humana, mais plástico o animal carrega”, explicou ao g1 Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, uma das autoras do estudo e pesquisadora da Universidade da Colúmbia Britânica, no Canadá.

Segundo ela, um dos resultados que mais chamou atenção foi encontrar o mesmo padrão em animais com hábitos alimentares muito diferentes .

“As antas comem plantas, os tamanduás comem formigas e cupins e ainda engolem muita terra no processo”, explica. “Isso sugere que a dieta não é o único fator por trás da exposição aos microplásticos.”

O resultado mais surpreendente, porém, apareceu no Pantanal.

Todos os animais analisados na região apresentaram microplásticos no sangue, inclusive indivíduos que viviam a mais de 65 quilômetros de áreas construídas e a mais de 112 quilômetros de uma instalação de resíduos .

Para Ferraz, o resultado mostra que a influência da poluição por plástico pode ultrapassar bastante os locais diretamente modificados pelo homem.

Ainda não é possível dizer, contudo, exatamente como essas partículas chegaram ao organismo dos animais.

Elas podem ter sido ingeridas pela água ou pelos alimentos ou até inaladas , mas o estudo analisou o plástico presente no sangue e não mediu diretamente sua concentração no ambiente.

“Pode ser pela comida, pela água ou pelo ar, mas nosso estudo mediu o plástico no sangue, não no ambiente, então não dá para afirmar”, diz Ferraz.

Os tipos de plástico encontrados também variaram entre os locais estudados.

No Cerrado, onde a área analisada é marcada pela agricultura, apareceram em maior proporção materiais como PVC e poliestireno , usados, entre outras aplicações, em tubulações, máquinas e embalagens.

Na área estudada da Amazônia, foi mais frequente a poliamida, usada em redes e cordas de pesca.

Já no Pantanal apareceram mais politetrafluoretileno , conhecido como teflon , e polipropileno .

Os pesquisadores, porém, ressaltam que essas diferenças não permitem apontar diretamente a origem das partículas.

Os três locais tinham tamanhos de amostra diferentes e foram analisados como estudos de caso, e não como um retrato completo de cada bioma.

O trabalho também não avaliou se a quantidade de microplásticos encontrada provocou danos à saúde dos animais.

Segundo Ferraz, ainda não existe um valor de referência que indique que determinada concentração é segura ou perigosa para animais silvestres.

Estudos de laboratório indicam que partículas pequenas podem atravessar membranas e se acumular em tecidos, mas ainda não se sabe se os mesmos efeitos ocorrem nas condições encontradas na natureza.

A pesquisadora também evita afirmar que os resultados comprovam que os microplásticos já estejam disseminados por toda a fauna brasileira.

Ainda assim, ela considera que encontrar partículas em espécies diferentes e em três regiões do país, inclusive no Pantanal, representa “ um forte indício ” de que a contaminação pode estar bastante espalhada.

“Para confirmar, precisamos estudar mais espécies e mais regiões”, diz.

Os autores afirmam ainda que o resultado também traz implicações para a conservação, porque mostra que proteger apenas o habitat imediato de um animal pode não ser suficiente para evitar a exposição a determinados poluentes.

No estudo, animais que viviam em áreas menos alteradas apresentavam quantidades menores de microplásticos do que aqueles mais próximos de infraestrutura humana.

Por isso, os pesquisadores defendem que melhorar a gestão de resíduos e considerar a localização de aterros e outras instalações próximas a áreas de fauna podem ajudar a reduzir essa exposição.

“Existe também uma difusão desses poluentes: o plástico chega aos animais mesmo quando o habitat está relativamente preservado, e isso também precisa entrar na conta das estratégias de conservação”, afirma Ferraz.

Segundo ela, as próximas pesquisas devem tentar responder duas questões centrais: de onde exatamente vêm esses microplásticos e quais efeitos eles podem provocar na saúde de animais silvestres que vivem livres na natureza.

articles.title: Greve geral na Espanha: manifestantes e polícia entram em confronto | G1
articles.standfirst: Na capital, Madri, os protestos bloquearam a Gran Via, uma das principais ruas comerciais da capital, e forçaram o fechamento de lojas.
articles.summary: Na capital, Madri, os protestos bloquearam a Gran Via, uma das principais ruas comerciais da capital, e forçaram o fechamento de lojas.
articles.body:
Manifestantes entraram em confronto com a polícia durante um protesto em Madri , a capital da Espanha, nesta quarta-feira (11), dia de greve geral no país.

Segurando cartazes reclamando do alto custo de vida e da grave crise habitacional no país, e pedindo melhores salários, os grevistas bloquearam a Gran Via, uma das principais ruas comerciais da capital espanhola, e forçaram o fechamento de estabelecimentos comerciais.

Grandes lojas de departamento como Primark, H&M e Pull & Bear fecharam as portas em meio a uma forte presença da polícia antimotim.

Loja de departamento fechada por causa de protesto em Madri — Foto: REUTERS/Juan Barbosa

Em Barcelona , muitas lojas também fecharam e usaram tábuas para se protegerem de vandalismo.

Imagens feitas ao vivo no protesto em Madri registraram o momento em que policiais usaram cassetetes e bombas de gás lacrimogêneo para conter os manifestantes (veja acima) .

Agentes da polícia detêm um manifestante durante uma greve geral nacional de 24 horas em Madri — Foto: REUTERS/Susana Vera

Milhões de trabalhadores espanhóis estão em greve - a primeira na Espanha em 14 anos - para exigir que o governo resolva a crise habitacional do país.

Manifestantes ajudam uma mulher que foi atingida por spray de pimenta pela polícia, durante uma greve geral nacional de 24 horas, em Madri — Foto: REUTERS/Susana Vera

A greve geral está causando atrasos no sistema de transporte público e desacelerando as fábricas. Muitas escolas e universidades fecharam ou estão funcionando com capacidade reduzida.

Em Madri, a greve geral se soma a uma já em andamento, iniciada por professores há quase um mês, reivindicando melhores condições de trabalho. A capital também teve os ônibus urbanos afetados por causa do movimento dos sindicatos e pelas fortes chuvas registradas pela manhã.

Em Barcelona, ​​a segunda maior cidade do país, o transporte público estava parado ou enfrentava longos atrasos no horário de pico da manhã.

Uma mulher caminha pela estação ferroviária de Atocha durante uma greve geral nacional em protesto contra a crise habitacional no país, em Madri, Espanha. — Foto: AP/Francisco Seco

Os dois principais sindicatos que convocaram a greve, UGT e CCOO, afirmaram em comunicado que houve ampla participação, "com paralisações significativas em setores estratégicos" — 90% nos setores automotivo e portuário, 85% na indústria da carne, 82% na coleta de resíduos e 75% no setor de energia.

“É extremamente importante lembrar às pessoas que nós, os trabalhadores — que também somos inquilinos ou pagamos hipotecas — somos os que têm o poder de interromper a produção e paralisar a economia”, disse Sandra Mora, porta-voz do Sindicato dos Inquilinos, à rádio nacional RNE.

articles.title: Concurso Ipam Porto Velho: MPRO recomenda ajustes e revisão de cargos | G1
articles.standfirst: MPRO identifica indícios de que cargos comissionados do instituto estariam exercendo funções técnicas e permanentes. Essas atividades devem ser desempenhadas por servidores concursados.
articles.summary: Após identificar indícios de irregularidades, o MPRO recomendou que o Ipam de Porto Velho revise cargos comissionados e ajuste o edital do concurso público 2026.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público de Rondônia (MPRO) expediu recomendações administrativas ao Instituto de Previdência e Assistência dos Servidores do Município de Porto Velho (Ipam) após investigar a criação, ampliação e ocupação de cargos comissionados no órgão, além da realização do concurso público regido pelo Edital nº 01/2026. O caso foi divulgado na terça-feira (10).

A recomendação foi encaminhada à presidência do Ipam, ao prefeito de Porto Velho, à Câmara Municipal, à Procuradoria-Geral do Município e aos setores responsáveis pelo planejamento orçamentário.

O documento foi expedido pela 6ª Promotoria de Justiça de Porto Velho após o MPRO identificar indícios de que cargos comissionados do instituto estariam exercendo funções técnicas e permanentes. Segundo o órgão, essas atividades devem ser desempenhadas por servidores concursados , conforme prevê a Constituição Federal.

Diante disso, o Ministério Público recomendou a revisão da estrutura administrativa do Ipam para verificar possíveis sobreposições de atribuições e adequar cargos em desacordo com a legislação.

O órgão também solicitou documentos que comprovem a regularidade orçamentária da criação e ocupação desses cargos , incluindo a previsão de gastos e o cumprimento das exigências da Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal.

Concurso público deve ter ajustes no edital

Em relação ao concurso público , o MPRO recomendou ajustes no edital para garantir mais transparência e segurança jurídica. Entre as medidas apontadas estão a definição clara do número de vagas imediatas e para cadastro de reserva, a revisão das regras de cotas para pessoas com deficiência, negros e idosos, além da correção de inconsistências identificadas no texto.

O órgão também orientou a adoção de medidas de fiscalização na aplicação das provas, na análise de recursos e na verificação da autenticidade dos títulos apresentados pelos candidatos.

Segundo o Ministério Público, as recomendações têm como objetivo corrigir irregularidades na estrutura de cargos do Ipam e prevenir problemas relacionados ao concurso público e ao orçamento municipal. O órgão destacou que, até o momento, não há responsabilização de servidores ou gestores.

Em nota, o instituto afirmou que o concurso público segue normalmente, com inscrições abertas, e destacou que o certame é o primeiro para cargos efetivos desde a criação da autarquia.

Segundo o Ipam, alguns ajustes no edital já haviam sido identificados e solicitados antes da recomendação do MPRO, enquanto os demais apontamentos estão sendo analisados pelas áreas técnicas e jurídicas.

O Ipam também informou que já conduz estudos para reorganizar a estrutura administrativa, com revisão das atribuições dos cargos e planejamento da transição para a atuação de servidores efetivos. A autarquia afirmou vai manter colaboração com os órgãos de controle e que eventuais retificações no concurso serão divulgadas pelos canais oficiais.

articles.title: Seca na Paraíba atinge quase 92% do território, aponta Monitor | G1
articles.standfirst: Em setembro de 2026, o monitoramento voltou a registrar seca grave no estado, que não era observada desde abril, e que afeta 37,90% da área.
articles.summary: Seca na Paraíba atinge 91,8% do território e volta ao nível grave; levantamento mostra que 183 municípios enfrentaram o fenômeno nos últimos anos.
articles.body:
Seca atinge quase 92% do território da Paraíba, aponta Monitor de Secas — Foto: Reprodução/Monitor de Secas

A seca atinge 91,80% do território da Paraíba, segundo dados do mês de setembro de 2026 do Monitor de Secas, da Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA). O monitoramento voltou a registrar seca grave, que não era observada desde abriu, e que afeta 37,90% da área.

Segundo o Monitor, apenas 8,20% da área do estado está sem seca. Em relação aos meses de abril e agosto de 2026, a seca avançou e território não afetado pelo fenômeno diminuiu.

Nos meses de janeiro a março, a seca atingia todo o território paraibano, com presença de seca extrema nos dois primeiros meses do ano.

O Monitor de Secas monitora mensalmente a situação da seca no país. Os dados são produzidos por um grupo de instituições e pessoas de diversos Estados e do Governo Federal, de forma colaborativa e voluntária.

Mais de 180 municípios da PB enfrentaram secas entre 2021 e 2024, diz IBGE

Dos 223 municípios do estado, 183 enfrentaram seca entre os anos de 2021 e 2024, segundo dados da Pesquisa de Informações Básicas Municipais (MUNIC) 2025 divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) nesta quarta-feira (11). Em 2024, 147 cidades emitiram decreto de emergência ou calamidade.

Também em 2024, ano de maior impacto da seca, 70 municípios apresentaram plano de contingência e prevenção contra a seca.

Além da seca, a pesquisa também contabiliza outros desastres naturais.

articles.title: Incêndio em Ilhabela atinge depósito de tintas no Barra Velha | G1
articles.standfirst: Fogo começou em cômodo que armazenava escadas, latas de tinta e outros objetos, no bairro Barra Velha.
articles.summary: O incêndio em Ilhabela atingiu um depósito de tintas e materiais no bairro Barra Velha, sendo controlado pelos Bombeiros após o desligamento da energia do imóvel.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu um cômodo usado como depósito de tintas e outros materiais em uma residência de Ilhabela (SP), na tarde desta quarta-feira (11). O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e conseguiu controlar as chamas.

Segundo os bombeiros, a ocorrência foi registrada por volta das 12h40, na Rua Amazonas, no bairro Barra Velha. O fogo começou em um cômodo utilizado para guardar materiais diversos, como escadas, latas de tinta e outros objetos.

Ao chegar ao endereço, a equipe desligou a energia elétrica do imóvel e iniciou o combate às chamas. O incêndio foi extinto às 13h21.

Após controlar o fogo, os bombeiros realizaram o trabalho de rescaldo, procedimento para evitar que as chamas voltem, e uma vistoria nas três residências existentes no local para verificar a possível presença de vítimas e identificar focos remanescentes.

As equipes também abriram as janelas dos imóveis para facilitar a saída da fumaça e a ventilação dos ambientes. A ocorrência foi encerrada sem registro de vítimas.

Bombeiros combateram incêndio em residência no bairro Barra Velha, em Ilhabela (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/Corpo de Bombeiros

articles.title: IMC não basta para saber quem tem obesidade e deixa escapar parte dos casos | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo publicado na Nature com 844 mil adultos mostra que olhar a gordura da barriga e a saúde dos órgãos revela mais pessoas com a doença. Cintura e exames simples entram na avaliação, afirma especialista.
articles.summary: Estudo publicado na Nature com 844 mil adultos mostra que olhar a gordura da barriga e a saúde dos órgãos revela mais pessoas com a doença. Cintura e exames simples entram na avaliação, afirma especialista.
articles.body:
Medir onde a gordura está no corpo e se ela já prejudica os órgãos identifica mais pessoas com obesidade do que o cálculo de peso e altura usado hoje, o índice de massa corporal (IMC).

Um estudo publicado nesta quarta-feira (11) na revista Nature, com 844.108 adultos da China, do Reino Unido, dos Estados Unidos e da Espanha, mostrou que o diagnóstico aumentou entre 3,3% e 7,4% quando essas informações foram somadas ao IMC.

A comparação foi feita com um modelo proposto em 2025 pela Comissão Lancet de Diabetes e Endocrinologia, que olha também para a distribuição da gordura e para o funcionamento dos órgãos. Os pesquisadores, liderados por An Pan, da Universidade de Ciência e Tecnologia de Huazhong, na China, e Francesco Rubino, do King’s College London, aplicaram o modelo em quatro grandes grupos de adultos, um em cada país.

O IMC errou nos dois sentidos, mas errou mais por não enxergar a doença. Ele deixou de reconhecer a obesidade em até 8,6% dos participantes e, em menor número, apontou a doença em quem não tinha.

O que a conta de peso e altura não mostra

O cálculo usa só o peso e a altura, e por isso trata do mesmo jeito corpos muito diferentes. Duas pessoas podem ter o mesmo IMC, uma com mais músculo e outra com mais gordura na barriga, e o resultado não distingue uma da outra.

O índice foi criado para descrever grupos de pessoas, e não para diagnosticar pacientes, explica Fernando Valente, coordenador do Departamento de Educação em Diabetes da Sociedade Brasileira de Diabetes e diretor do Departamento de Diabetes da Sociedade Brasileira de Endocrinologia e Metabologia.

Ele continua em uso porque é simples, barato e dá o mesmo resultado com médicos diferentes. Uma revisão de estudos citada por Valente mostrou que o IMC deixa de reconhecer cerca de metade das pessoas com muita gordura no corpo.

👴 Um idoso que perdeu músculo e ganhou gordura pode ter IMC considerado normal, e o mesmo acontece com algumas mulheres.

🏋️‍♂️ Um atleta, ao contrário, pode ter IMC alto por causa da massa muscular, sem excesso de gordura.

Os limites do índice também variam entre grupos étnicos: pessoas de origem asiática podem adoecer com IMC mais baixo do que o considerado de risco, enquanto, entre pessoas negras, o índice tende a indicar um risco maior do que o real.

A gordura que mais preocupa os médicos fica dentro da barriga, em volta dos órgãos. Ela causa inflamação no corpo, ao contrário da gordura sob a pele, que serve para guardar energia.

Quem tem pouco músculo, por sua vez, fica mais fraco, corre mais risco de cair e de ter doenças ligadas ao metabolismo, mas pesa menos na balança, o que esconde o problema.

Mesmo sem excesso de peso, tem a gordura que não é vista no espelho, mas que se acumula em órgãos como fígado e coração. — Foto: Divulgação

O modelo avaliado na Nature separa a obesidade em duas situações. Há o excesso de gordura que ainda não afetou nenhum órgão, chamado de obesidade pré-clínica, e o que já causa problemas que podem ser medidos, no coração, nos rins, no fígado ou nas articulações, ou que atrapalha tarefas do dia a dia, chamado de obesidade clínica. A explicação é de Valente, que usaria essas mesmas palavras com um paciente.

Os resultados mostraram que as duas situações são diferentes. A obesidade clínica esteve ligada a um risco de morte bem maior. Entre as pessoas com a forma pré-clínica, apenas de 10% a 30% passaram a ter danos nos órgãos ao longo de dez anos.

Isso não quer dizer que basta esperar, ressalta o médico. Quem já tem danos precisa de um tratamento mais intenso, com remédios ou cirurgia quando indicados. Quem ainda não tem recebe orientação para prevenir e fica em acompanhamento, com cuidado na alimentação, atividade física e controle da pressão, do açúcar no sangue e do colesterol.

obesidade — Foto: suriya - stock.adobe.com

Remédios para obesidade, cirurgia bariátrica e planos de saúde costumam usar o IMC para decidir quem pode ser tratado. Se o critério mudar, mais gente pode ter acesso, como quem tem IMC normal mas risco real e hoje fica sem cuidado, avalia Valente.

A mudança traz um risco: aumentar o número de diagnósticos e tratar de forma intensa quem ainda não tem danos, o que sobrecarregaria o sistema de saúde e os planos. Por isso, ele defende que a diferença entre as duas situações continue valendo na hora de decidir quem recebe o tratamento.

Para o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), o médico considera a mudança viável. Bastam uma fita métrica e os exames de sangue que já costumam ser pedidos, sem aparelhos de composição corporal como a bioimpedância.

A medida mais simples é a da cintura . Ela deve ter no máximo metade da altura, regra que vale para qualquer sexo e etnia. Quem mede 1,70 metro, por exemplo, deve ficar em até 85 centímetros de cintura.

Os médicos também avaliam a pressão e os exames de açúcar e de gordura no sangue, que revelam problemas mesmo quando o IMC está normal. Em alguns casos, pedem um ultrassom para ver se há gordura no fígado. O IMC segue útil como ponto de partida, mas não deve ser o único olhar. Vale prestar atenção também a sinais do dia a dia, como falta de fôlego, dor nas articulações e sono ruim.

Para os autores do estudo, incluir medidas de gordura e de funcionamento dos órgãos nas avaliações ajuda a orientar o tratamento de cada paciente e a definir políticas de saúde.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Tamanduá é flagrado em banquete de formigas no Pantanal | G1
articles.standfirst: Guia Fagner Almeida fez o registro na área do Refúgio Ecológico Caiman, em Miranda. O animal usa língua pegajosa e garras para capturar insetos sem destruir formigueiros.
articles.summary: O guia Fagner Almeida registrou o tamanduá-bandeira no Refúgio Ecológico Caiman, em Miranda, revelando como o animal usa garras e saliva para capturar insetos.
articles.body:
O guia de turismo Fagner Almeida gravou o momento em que um tamanduá-bandeira se alimenta de formigas na região do Refúgio Ecológico Caiman, em Miranda , município do Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul. O registro foi feito durante um percurso de observação de fauna e mostra o mamífero utilizando as garras e a língua para capturar os insetos no chão. Veja o vídeo acima.

No vídeo, o animal insere o focinho fino nos acessos do formigueiro e recolhe os insetos com rapidez antes de se deslocar para outra área da vegetação.

Mesmo com a rotina de trabalho na reserva pantaneira, o guia relata que a aproximação com a espécie revela detalhes novos sobre a fauna local.

"Sim, já havia visto antes. A cada encontro com esse animal, temos a oportunidade de observar comportamentos diferentes e aprender um pouco mais sobre seus hábitos", relata Fagner.

Tamanduá se alimenta de formigas e insetos. — Foto: Fagner alameida

O Tamanduá Bandeira consome cerca de 30 mil a 35 mil formigas e cupins por dia. Como não possui dentes, ele usa as garras para abrir cupinzeiros e formigueiros e introduz uma língua longa (que pode projetar até 60 cm) coberta de saliva pegajosa para capturar os insetos, engolindo-os inteiros.

Já o Tamanduá-mirim consegue comer até 9 mil insetos por dia, o que equivale a 1,5 kg de formigas e cupins, além de poder consumir larvas, mel e ovos.

Em parques ecológicos e zoológicos, ambas espécies têm a dieta adaptada para suprir os nutrientes necessários, incluindo oferta ocasional de frutas e insetos para enriquecimento ambiental.

A presença do tamanduá-bandeira na região pantaneira atua no controle populacional de insetos, mantendo a estrutura da vegetação e o equilíbrio do ecossistema local.

articles.title: Leão XIV reúne 2 milhões de fiéis, visita presídio e segue ao Peru | G1
articles.standfirst: Visita à Basílica de Lujan encerra a etapa argentina da viagem de 12 dias do pontífice na América Latina. Nesta quarta (11), Leão XIV desembarca no Peru, país onde foi missionário por mais de 20 anos em seu primeiro retorno desde o início do pontificado.
articles.summary: O papa Leão XIV encerrou sua agenda na Argentina com missa campal em Luján e visita a um presídio. Ele agora segue para o Peru, onde viveu por 20 anos e encontrará Keiko Fujimori.
articles.body:
O papa Leão XIV chega no papamóvel para celebrar a missa em frente à Basílica de Nossa Senhora de Luján, na primeira visita papal à Argentina desde 1987, como parte de sua viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul, em Luján, Argentina. — Foto: Reuters

O papa Leão XIV encerrou sua visita à Argentina nesta quarta-feira (11) com uma missa campal para mais de 2 milhões de pessoas no santuário de Nossa Senhora de Luján, o mais importante local de devoção católica da Argentina.

Na segunda-feira (9), o papa reuniu mais de 2,5 milhões de fiéis em uma celebração em Buenos Aires. Entre os presentes estava o presidente argentino, Javier Milei. A missa na capital argentina foi o maior evento individual de seus 18 meses de pontificado.

Javier Milei recebe o papa Leão XIV em Buenos Aires neste domingo (8) — Foto: Agustin Marcarian/Reuters

Após a celebração, o pontífice embarca para o Peru, em um retorno emocionante para o primeiro cidadão peruano a liderar a Igreja Católica — nascido nos EUA, Leão XIV viveu como missionário no país latino por mais de 20 anos e recebeu a cidadania local.

A viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul se encerrará no dia 17 de novembro.

Em Lujan, multidões se estenderam por quilômetros ao redor do santuário, com pessoas se aglomerando contra as barreiras de segurança, cantando "Leão, Leão, Leão" e agitando bandeiras brancas e amarelas do Vaticano enquanto ele chegava em um papamóvel aberto.

Antes da missa, o papa visitou uma das maiores penitenciárias da Argentina, onde abraçou detentos e pediu aos guardas que tratassem os presos com humanidade.

O forte discurso do pontífice em prol da caridade ocorre em meio a críticas da Igreja aos cortes nos programas sociais promovidos pelo presidente Javier Milei.

Papa Leão XIV discursa durante sua visita ao Complexo Penitenciário Federal em Buenos Aires, Argentina. — Foto: Reuters

A visita de Leão XIV ao Peru deve incluir cenas emocionantes, com o papa visitando antigos amigos e passando três dias na cidade de Chiclayo, onde foi bispo de 2015 a 2023.

A viagem também é um teste, que vai medir o quão diretamente ele está disposto a se envolver na política de sua nação adotiva.

Leão XIV deve pousar na Base Aérea de Callao, no Peru, às 17h30 do horário local desta quarta, 19h no horário de Brasília.

Após uma breve cerimônia de boas-vindas, ele seguirá para o palácio presidencial para um discurso muito aguardado à presidente Keiko Fujimori, eleita este ano em uma das eleições mais disputadas da história do Peru, marcada por acusações de fraude e atrasos na apuração dos votos.

Keiko Fujimori assumiu a presidência do Peru ao vencer as eleições com a promessa de 'braço forte' no setor de segurança, seguindo outros governantes de direita da região — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

Fujimori é filha do ex-presidente Alberto Fujimori, que governou o país de 1990 a 2000 e faleceu em 2024. Sua vitória marcou o retorno de uma das dinastias políticas mais influentes e controversas do Peru.

Em 2017, Leão XIV, então conhecido como Bispo Robert Prevost, criticou o indulto concedido ao falecido presidente Fujimori.

Ele afirmou que o ex-presidente, que havia sido condenado por graves violações dos direitos humanos, deveria buscar pessoalmente o perdão das vítimas para que o Peru alcançasse uma reconciliação genuína.

Durante sua campanha presidencial, Keiko Fujimori se apoiou fortemente no legado político de seu pai.

O Peru preparou-se com fervor para o retorno do agora pontífice: uma estátua de 14 metros representando Leão com os braços abertos foi erguida em Callao; comerciantes em Lima vendem camisas e lembranças com o tema do papa; e as detentas da maior prisão feminina do país costuraram bonecas de veludo com a sua imagem.

Uma estátua gigante do papa Leão é inaugurada em Callao, no Peru, em 9 de novembro de 2026, às vésperas da visita do pontífice ao país. — Foto: REUTERS/Daniel Becerril

Martin Cassinelli, analista do Atlantic Council, afirmou que as raízes peruanas de Leão XIV lhe conferem uma capacidade incomum de falar sobre o passado político do país.

"Não existe outro país em que o papa esteja tão sintonizado com a política interna quanto o Peru", disse Cassinelli. "Se há algo que possa potencialmente entrar em conflito com o atual governo Fujimori, seria uma reflexão sobre o passado."

As relações entre o governo do falecido Fujimori e setores da Igreja Católica eram frequentemente tensas, particularmente em relação aos direitos humanos durante a luta do Estado contra a insurgência maoísta do Sendero Luminoso.

Figuras da Igreja também se opuseram à anistia concedida em 1995 a membros das forças de segurança acusados ​​de violações de direitos humanos.

articles.title: Mousse de acerola com geleia: aprenda a receita da Chef Eva da Luz | G1
articles.standfirst: Chefe de cozinha Eva da Luz mostra o passo a passo da sobremesa. A receita é simples, refrescante e traz um sabor marcante.
articles.summary: Mousse de acerola é a aposta da chef Eva da Luz para uma sobremesa rica em vitamina C que utiliza frutas frescas, leite condensado e uma calda de geleia caseira.
articles.body:
Famosa por ser rica em vitamina C, a acerola é o ingrediente principal de uma sobremesa ensinada pela chefe de cozinha Eva da Luz. A receita de mousse com geleia de acerola é simples, refrescante e traz um sabor marcante.

540 g de açúcar (dividido em duas partes)

Mousse com geleia de acerola — Foto: Reprodução / TV Grande Rio

Geleia: Para a geleia, coloque em uma panela 800 g de acerola, 500 ml de água e 240 g de açúcar. Leve ao fogo e mexa até a fruta começar a desmanchar. Em seguida, bata a mistura no liquidificador e passe por uma peneira. Devolva o líquido à panela e adicione os 300 g de açúcar restantes. Cozinhe em fogo baixo até a geleia ganhar consistência, mas sem deixar engrossar muito. Depois, leve à geladeira por cerca de 30 minutos para esfriar.

Mousse: No liquidificador, bata o leite condensado, o creme de leite, 500 g da geleia pronta e o suco de meio limão. Misture até ficar bem cremoso. Após bater, leve a mousse à geladeira por mais 30 minutos.

Montagem: Na hora de servir, coloque o restante da geleia por cima da sobremesa. Além de decorar, a cobertura reforça o sabor da fruta.

articles.title: Embaixador russo nos EUA morre aos 66 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Putin nomeou Alexander Darchiev como embaixador em Washington em março de 2025, com a missão de liderar uma reaproximação com o governo Trump.
articles.summary: Causa da morte não foi informada. Putin nomeou Alexander Darchiev como embaixador em Washington em março de 2025, com a missão de liderar uma reaproximação com o governo Trump.
articles.body:
Alexander Darchiev, embaixador da Rússia nos EUA — Foto: Divulgação/Embaixada da Rússia nos EUA

O embaixador da Rússia nos Estados Unidos, Alexander Darchiev, morreu aos 66 anos, informou o Ministério das Relações Exteriores russo nesta quarta-feira (11).

Em comunicado, o ministério afirmou que Darchiev "morreu repentinamente", mas não divulgou a causa da morte.

Putin nomeou Darchiev, um diplomata veterano conhecido por suas críticas públicas ao Ocidente, como embaixador em Washington em março de 2025, com a missão de liderar uma reaproximação com o governo Trump - iniciativa que tem causado apreensão na Ucrânia e em países europeus.

O ministério das Relações Exteriores russo afirmou que Darchiev era "um diplomata excepcional, líder experiente, colega gentil e mentor". O comunicado também descreve o embaixador como um "profissional da mais alta categoria e um brilhante especialista em assuntos americanos".

Antes de assumir o cargo de embaixador, Darchiev ocupou diversos postos no Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, segundo a Embaixada do país nos Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Veterans Day spurs cowboy chef to fight to keep America's heroes from being forgotten
articles.summary: "Cowboy" Kent Rollins and wife Shannon cooked corn fritters, succotash and apple fritters with veterans through a therapeutic cooking program event.
articles.body: For "Cowboy" Kent Rollins and his wife, Shannon, cooking with veterans shows how a simple recipe can offer structure, confidence and connection after military service. The couple saw that firsthand while spending time in the kitchen with veterans through Veterans Equine Therapeutic Services (VETS), a nonprofit program that began with equine therapy and has expanded to include activities such as archery and cooking. "Food brings people together," Shannon Rollins told Fox News Digital. CELEBRITY CHEF SAYS MILITARY LESSON IS KEY TO KEEPING FAMILIES TOGETHER Veterans who gathered to cook were able to work in teams, share stories and laugh, she said. "Sometimes it's not about the food. I think that's the best part." The event with VETS was filmed Sept. 13 and 14 at Grijalva Cattle Company in Connecticut for the third season of the Outdoor Channel's "Cast Iron Cowboy," Kent and Shannon Rollins' TV show. VETS' Cowboy Kitchen, a program offered by the nonprofit, was actually inspired by Kent Rollins' Red River Ranch Chuck Wagon Cooking School in Oklahoma. The program uses cooking to help veterans build confidence, self-reliance and connection. Some of the veterans the Rollins met with had little cooking experience, Kent Rollins told Fox News Digital. He noticed that they followed recipes before becoming comfortable enough to get creative. COWBOY CHEF SAYS PHONES AND SCREENS AT DINNER ARE TEARING AMERICAN FAMILIES APART "They change things, they add things, they adapt, overcome — just like they always have in life," he said. Shannon Rollins also saw a connection between the structure of a recipe and the transition from military life back into civilian life. CELEBRITY CHEF SAYS PEOPLE HAVE SOUTHERN FOOD ALL WRONG, SHARES WHAT HER FAMILY ATE "When you get out of the military, life can feel chaotic," she said. "With recipes, it's a format. You follow the format, and you have an end result and that feels good." For Veterans Day, the Rollinses are highlighting the kind of familiar, hearty food that can be made with everyday ingredients. "You can't get full on fancy," Kent Rollins said. "This is food that you have in your house." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER One crowd favorite was his wife's corn fritters. Shannon Rollins said she makes them with flour, corn, a little sugar and baking powder, with green chile or jalapeño and onion as optional additions. She then forms the mixture into small patties and fries them. "She was frying them as fast as she could, and they [were] running out just as fast as they hit the pan," Kent Rollins said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The couple also served succotash and apple fritters to the vets, leaning into fall ingredients and regional flavors. Kent Rollins said the food was meant to be hearty and filling, while Shannon Rollins noted that familiar ingredients can help keep meals affordable. "Let's take time to listen to them. Let's hear what they got to say." Even with canned goods, home cooks can make small tweaks to boost the flavor, Kent Rollins said. The goal, he added, is food that is "easy on the pocket." articles.title: Asian shops targeted as Eswatini cracks down on illegal foreign businesses
articles.summary: The law follows the growth of foreign-owned businesses in rural areas.
articles.body:
Businesses owned by Asian nationals are being closed across Eswatini, previously known as Swaziland, as the government cracks down on foreign-owned enterprises.

It follows parliament's approval of a law that seeks to increase ownership and participation by emaSwati, as citizens of the kingdom are known.

The legislation comes after complaints from local traders that foreign-owned businesses are encroaching on traditional retail markets, increasing competition and threatening livelihoods.

South Africa has witnessed more severe enforcement action, including raids, arrests and the disruption of foreign-run informal businesses, while Kenya has also stepped up action against foreign traders.

Eswatini is a small landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, led by absolute monarch King Mswati III, where about 70% of its population live below the poverty line.

Those angered by economic hardships have become increasingly vocal in demanding political reform.

Pro-democracy protests broke out in 2021- and the royal family has faced criticism by activists for its extravagant spending as many emaSwati with a job work in neighbouring South Africa and send their earnings home.

The government says the new law is intended to expand economic opportunities, amid concerns that poverty and hunger could fuel further political unrest.

But the implementation of the Citizen Economic Empowerment Act has sparked a heated debate in Eswatini's parliament, with MPs divided over how quickly foreign businesses owners should be required to leave.

On Tuesday, Mbabane East MP Welcome Dlamini said that officials from the trade ministry had already begun enforcing the law by closing Asian-owned shops.

Hhohho Regional MP Tanele Magagula called for immediate action, saying: "Businesses owned by foreigners in the rural areas must be seized immediately."

Dlamini questioned whether local entrepreneurs were ready to take over the businesses, arguing that foreigners should be given time to train their successors.

"Why can't we give the Asians or foreigners at least three years before 'kicking them' out so that emaSwati can learn to run the businesses?" he asked.

Magagula rejected the suggestion, questioning why struggling local traders should have to wait while struggling economically.

"Why must we wait for three years while emaSwati suffer?" she asked.

Parliament subsequently agreed that foreign business owners should be given at least 12 months to leave.

However, unless the law is formally amended to reflect that timeline, the ministry could continue enforcing its provisions.

The closures follow inspections launched by the trade ministry in August. Some businesses inspected in areas such as the capital, Mbabane, were found to be fully compliant.

Nonetheless the inspections also raised concerns about working conditions and administrative practices at foreign-owned enterprises, including complaints by employees over days off, annual leave and overtime. At least one case remains under investigation.

The crackdown comes amid growing pressure on foreign-owned businesses elsewhere in the region, particularly in South Africa, which has experienced repeated outbreaks of xenophobic violence, often targeting African migrants.

Anti-migrant groups there set 30 June as a deadline for undocumented migrants to leave the country - and their campaigns this year has often been accompanied by violence and attacks on foreign-owned businesses.

Two Ghanaian and two Nigerian nationals were reported killed amid the tensions.

Kenya has also stepped up enforcement against foreign traders , bringing renewed attention to the treatment of foreign nationals and their businesses across the region.

articles.title: Meet Justin Cheung, the Canadian entrepreneur who turned discarded orange and lemon peels from grocery stores into candied snacks and built a business that generated $100,000 in revenue
articles.summary: Canadian entrepreneur Justin Cheung has discovered a way to turn grocery-store food waste into a business opportunity, by turning discarded orange and
articles.body: Canadian entrepreneur Justin Cheung has discovered a way to turn grocery-store food waste into a business opportunity, by turning discarded orange and lemon peels into sweet and sour snacks. His company, Second Savor, makes candied and dehydrated citrus products from the waste of juice companies. A sustainability project by a Simon Fraser University student has turned into a growing snack brand, with products appearing in grocery stores. BCBusiness reports the company made $100,000 in revenue during its most recent fiscal year, a major milestone for its young founder.Justin Cheung turned discarded citrus peels into a snack businessThe idea behind Second Savour came from Cheung's interest in reducing food waste and a snack he remembered enjoying during his childhood in Asia. As reported by BCBusiness, Cheung was just 18 when he joined an extracurricular sustainability project at Simon Fraser University's Beedie School of Business. He began exploring whether discarded food could be converted into something consumers would actually want to buy.The concept centred on citrus peels left behind by grocery stores and juice producers. Rather than allowing the material to go to waste, Cheung developed a process to make candied, dehydrated peels into snacks. The result became Citrus Treats by Second Savour, a product line manufactured and distributed in British Columbia.The business also established connections with Save-On-Foods and Chasers, a cold-pressed juice wholesaler, to obtain discarded orange and lemon peels. This arrangement gave the company access to ingredients while helping suppliers manage material they otherwise had to dispose of.From a student initiative to a growing food brandSecond Savour did not begin as an established business with significant sales. It was originally part of Enactus, a student entrepreneurship initiative at SFU, where the founding team developed the concept. Its first year brought in only a few hundred dollars.According to Cobuu Ventures' September 2026 interview with Cheung, the venture generated approximately $460 in its first 12 months before the original team left. Cheung decided to take responsibility for the project and set himself a target of reaching $50,000 in revenue by the end of the following year.The challenge was not simply developing a product. He also had to rebuild the team, find financial support and establish a way to sell the snacks. Cobuu Ventures reported that Second Savour generated approximately $70,000 in revenue in 2025, starting the year with around $3,000.BCBusiness subsequently reported that the company reached $100,000 in its most recent fiscal year, demonstrating that the venture had moved beyond its modest student-project beginnings.What makes Second Savour's citrus snacks differentThe company's products use citrus peels that juicing businesses would otherwise discard. Instead of relying on fresh fruit for the entire product, Second Savour gives the leftover peel another purpose by turning it into an edible snack.Cobuu Ventures describes its current range as including sweet and sour orange, sour lemon and bittersweet grapefruit varieties. The products are sold under the Citrus Treats by Second Savour name, bringing an unusual ingredient to the grocery snack aisle.The business has also been exploring additional products. According to Cobuu Ventures, Second Savour has been developing dark chocolate-covered orange and white chocolate-covered lemon snacks with a Vancouver chocolate company. The venture has also been pursuing opportunities involving other grocery retailers, including IGA and Fresh St. Market.Cheung has acknowledged that sustainability alone does not persuade every customer to purchase food.How did Cheung build the business while studyingBuilding Second Savour required Cheung to manage his education alongside the demands of running a food company. Simon Fraser University's Beedie School of Business reported in February 2026 that he was still completing his undergraduate studies while leading the venture.The university also highlighted his participation in its Charles Chang Institute for Entrepreneurship and its entrepreneurship co-operative programme. The programme provided a salaried work term, mentorship and opportunities to test the business idea, helping Cheung move beyond a student initiative.According to SFU Beedie, his working hours increased considerably during the experience. articles.title: Chile transport workers protest over surging fuel prices
articles.summary: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.
articles.body:
Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.

Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.

They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.

Talks between government officials and protest leaders have so far failed to reach a resolution, with another meeting expected to take place on Wednesday.

The protest is being organised by the ⁠Fuerza del Norte trade union, which represents around 80% of Chile's lorry drivers, and the No+TAG civic protest ​movement.

"There is no point of agreement with the government that could offer any perspective to find solutions for everyone," Andrés Alarcón, a spokesman for No+TAG, said after talks broke down on Tuesday, adding "the strike continues".

Economy Minister Daniel Mas called for further dialogue, but warned "at some point, we will have to clear the highways".

He stressed the protests were impacting economic activity and exports, saying "we need to get the country moving again".

The government of President José Antonio Kast has faced public discontent over fuel prices for months.

The average price of diesel has risen 74% since March, according to industry groups.

Juan Cornejo, the president of the Association of Intercity Bus Owners, which represents 14 mid-sized companies, told AFP that "we've reached our limit".

"We've spent more than a month working with negative numbers," he added.

Lorry driver Claudio Elguezabal, who took part in a protest near the capital, Santiago, on Tuesday morning, said the situation was unsustainable.

"Right now I'm not making any profit. Sometimes you even have to put in your own money to cover the client," AFP quoted the 47-year-old as saying.

articles.body: Iran will not allow even a single particle of its enriched nuclear material to leave the country and will retaliate if the United States launches fresh strikes against the Islamic Republic, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said.Speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV, Rezaei's remarks came after US officials played down the need for further military action against Iran.Analysts have also pointed to a more conciliatory tone from President Donald Trump since Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.Rezaei said there were currently no negotiations between Tehran and Washington. He warned that any fresh US attacks would be met with retaliation."Any new US attacks will also be met with targeting US bases far away," he said.Iran's Supreme Leader has directed that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium must not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources told Reuters in May.The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60%, a level far higher than required for civilian use, when Israel and the US attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. articles.title: ELI FEDERMAN: A boycott backfired when Philadelphia showed up for Jewish businesses
articles.summary: Anti-Israel protesters targeted Jewish-owned restaurants in Philadelphia with a boycott, but the community packed those businesses in a show of solidarity.
articles.body: The best response to antisemitism isn’t censorship. It’s philosemitism and exposing the truth. I learned about the protests targeting Jewish-owned restaurants in Philadelphia on Nov. 8 when my friend Ari Engel posted on social media about going out to eat to support those establishments. They wanted to discourage people from patronizing these businesses. PHILLY DSA DECRIES BACKLASH OVER BOYCOTT TARGETING JEWISH EATERIES Instead, the community turned their boycott upside down with a deluge of support and patronage for those Jewish-owned businesses. The timing of the protest was chilling as it took place on the eve of the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, when Nazis attacked Jewish businesses, shattered storefronts and terrorized Jewish communities across Germany and Austria. Hundreds of people showed up, packed restaurants and formed lines around city blocks. One restaurant worried it wouldn’t have enough food to serve everyone. The protesters wanted to drive customers away. Instead, they drove customers in. I’M AN ARAB MUSLIM — I STILL DON’T UNDERSTAND THE ANTISEMITIC BDS MOVEMENT There’s a profound lesson here about the power of free expression. articles.title: No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister
articles.summary: Police Scotland said at least 1,000 schools received the email but the warnings were immediately assessed as hoaxes.
articles.body:
Scotland's education secretary has said there is no risk to the public after schools across the country were targeted with a fresh wave of hoax bomb threats, less than a month after a previous alert.

At least 1,000 schools received the hoax email, though police and the government said there was nothing within them to suggest a credible threat.

Government minister Mairi McAllan told parliament the situation was "very much in hand".

Specialist cyber-crime officers are working to identify the source of the messages, which were sent to both primary and secondary schools.

Similar "bogus" emails were sent to 300 schools in Northern Ireland , while schools in Italy also received threats.

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Sutherland told the BBC Scotland News that the police were able to assess the threat as a hoax in around an hour and urged parents not to keep their children away from school.

He said: "First and foremost, I'll be sending my daughter to school tomorrow. I think what is important is that we continue to be vigilant, but we are not alarmed.

"We have carried out a significant amount of checks on all of the information we have gathered so far and there is nothing to suggest there is a credible threat and there is no requirement to keep children away from education settings."

He said officers believed that the email was sent by the same source as emails sent to schools in Northern Ireland and elsewhere in the UK but it was "too early to say" who could be behind it.

"We will be working with partners across the UK and internationally to carry out a joined-up investigation," he added.

More than 300 calls to police after hoax bomb threats at schools

'Large number' of schools sent threatening email

Hundreds of Italian schools hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax

The education secretary told MSPs that she had held a meeting with police and local authorities.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," Mairi McAllan said.

"I would take this opportunity to repeat Police Scotland's advice that there is nothing to suggest any threats to the public from the content of the emails."

The cabinet secretary added there was a "considerable amount of work" ongoing by Police Scotland and partners across the UK to "understand the motivations and the individuals behind this".

Most local authorities contacted by BBC Scotland said schools were operating as normal but some confirmed pupils had been evacuated.

More than 300 calls were made to police when a similar message was sent to schools around the country on 19 October.

In many areas, pupils were off due to half-term holidays.

On Wednesday the majority of schools in Dumfries and Galloway received the email and some were evacuated as a precaution.

A spokesperson for the local authority said: "Each school community/setting is unique and as such has its own way of supporting and reassuring learners and staff.

"We also know that local police have attended some school settings in a community capacity to assist and reassure."

In Edinburgh Queensferry High School was evacuated and pupils were sent home.

Highland Council confirmed a number of its schools "made the decision to activate their emergency protocols".

Local authorities in Glasgow, Edinburgh, East Lothian, Aberdeenshire and Orkney also confirmed their schools received the message.

In Northern Ireland, the Education Authority (EA) said the "message has similarities with a bogus threat sent last month" which was treated as a hoax by the (PSNI).

The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the email originated from outside the UK .

Italian reports said 280 school head teachers had received threats in recent days. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called a meeting of top ministers and intelligence chiefs over the issue.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday criticised the Congress over Sonia Gandhi’s remarks on Operation Blue Star, saying that she had given a “clean chit” to "the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs."“Congress leaders in Punjab must break their silence over Sonia Gandhi’s clean chit to those responsible for the killing of thousands of innocent Sikhs in 1984,” the former Punjab deputy chief minister said in a post on X.Badal also claimed that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," released in India on Tuesday, contained an “admission” that her husband, then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, had “purposely and personally” decided against deploying Army units in Delhi to protect the Sikh community.Also Read | Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riots“This finally provides the clinching evidence of the Congress government’s patronage of the anti-Sikh massacre. The Congress government could send a Sikh general to lead Operation Blue Star at Sachkhand Sri Harmandir Sahib and Sri Akal Takht Sahib, but would not deploy Sikh Army personnel to protect innocent Sikhs in 1984?” he asked.The SAD chief was referring to retired lieutenant general Kuldeep Singh Brar, who commanded the Army's Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab.Badal further asked whether Punjab Congress leaders "endorse" Rajiv Gandhi's decision not to deploy the Army in Delhi."Do Punjab Congress leaders, including Sikh leaders, endorse this decision to leave innocent Sikhs at the mercy of marauding killers belonging to the Congress party and the government headed by Rajiv Gandhi? Will they ask Sonia Gandhi to explain why Rajiv Gandhi chose to stop the army deployment to save the lives of innocent Sikhs? Cowardly silence won’t do," he added.Anti-Sikh violence erupted across the country, particularly in Delhi, following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards on October 31, 1984. The assassination came months after Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in June 1984. Indira Gandhi was succeeded as Prime Minister by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi writes that her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, was “left with no choice” and “reluctantly” ordered the armed forces to launch Operation Blue Star.“Then intelligence reports informed Mrs Gandhi that the declaration of Khalistan as an independent state was imminent: Bhindranwale and his cohort planned to announce it and hoist its flag on the Har Mandir Sahib, the Golden Temple, on India's Independence Day, August 15,” she wrote.The former Congress president was referring to Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, who led the movement for a separate Sikh homeland of Khalistan. Bhindranwale and his supporters had been based inside the Golden Temple complex since 1982."Indira Gandhi's own relationship with the Sikh community was a deep and strong one, but the problem was spiralling; she held meetings until late hours of the night, hardly ate her meals and looked disturbed for days ... A week or so later, an intelligence official brought to Mrs Gandhi a film with harrowing visuals of the aftermath: As my mother-in-law watched the slow-moving record, I could see her face wet with tears -- tears of pain and regret, I think: sorrow at the manner which the siege had ended, at the large number of lives lost."Sonia Gandhi further wrote that Indira Gandhi had “flatly refused” to remove her Sikh bodyguards, a decision for which she ultimately “paid” with her life when two of them opened fire on her.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Indian-origin Naresh Bhatt found guilty of murdering wife in US after admitting to dismembering, dumping body in trash
articles.summary: Naresh Bhatt, an Indian-origin man, is found guilty of murdering his wife, Mamta Kafle Bhatt, in Virginia. Following a six-week trial, Bhatt confessed to dismembering her body while denying the act of murder.
articles.body: An Indian-origin man has been convicted of murdering his wife, Mamta Kafle Bhatt, in Virginia, more than two years after the 28-year-old nurse disappeared and her body was never recovered.A jury found Naresh Bhatt, 39, guilty of first-degree murder on Tuesday. He was also convicted of concealing and defiling his wife's body following a six-week trial, CNN reportedDuring his testimony, Bhatt admitted that he had dismembered his wife's body and disposed of her remains but denied killing her. He told the court that he found Mamta unconscious in their bedroom, surrounded by blood and vomit, and panicked when his attempts to revive her failed.Bhatt said he did not call emergency services and instead decided to dispose of her body. He initially considered throwing her remains into the Potomac River before attempting to put them in a rubbish bin. When they did not fit, he said he cut the body into pieces, placed the remains in several rubbish bags and disposed of them in a trash compactor at an apartment complex where he had previously lived.He also acknowledged taking the couple's then-11-month-old daughter with him on some of those trips.“I don’t know why I did not,” Bhatt told the court when asked why he had not called 911. “I tried to call. I was really scared. I don’t know why, something take over me. I was really, really panicked.”His testimony differed from his earlier public statements, in which he had denied knowing what happened to his wife. He had previously told police that he last saw her at the dinner table several days before reporting her missing.Mamta was last seen on July 27, 2024, at UVA Health Prince William Medical Center in Manassas, where she worked as a registered nurse, according to police and the hospital. A friend spoke to her by phone the following day, and she also posted a TikTok video featuring herself and her infant daughter, CNN affiliate WJLA reported.Her disappearance prompted an extensive search, with relatives raising concerns about her whereabouts. The family's worries were heightened by the fact that her daughter's first birthday was approaching.Following the verdict, Amy Ashworth, the commonwealth's attorney for Prince William County and the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park, said the decision marked an important step towards justice for the family.“This verdict represents an important measure of justice for Mamta Kafle Bhatt, whose life was tragically taken and whose family has endured more than two years of unimaginable pain and uncertainty,” Ashworth said in a statement as cited by the outlet.She added that she hoped the verdict would help the family move forward, knowing that Mamta's life mattered and that the person responsible had been held accountable.Bhatt faces a possible life sentence for first-degree murder, along with an additional five years for each of the two charges involving the handling of his wife's body. articles.title: Kenya's Ebola outbreak: Last patient discharged as countdown begins to be being declared free of the virus
articles.summary: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.
articles.body:
Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free.

It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died.

Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation.

"Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak.

"This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October.

All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission.

Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers.

Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday.

Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown.

Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries.

Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams.

The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country.

In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens.

Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings.

The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries.

Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there.

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June.

But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE.

The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures.

Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August.

The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

articles.title: France fears German long-range missiles could trigger nuclear escalation with Russia
articles.summary: Europe's efforts to build a stronger conventional deterrent against Russia are raising concerns as to whether a missile strike intended to weaken Moscow's
articles.body: Europe's efforts to build a stronger conventional deterrent against Russia are raising concerns as to whether a missile strike intended to weaken Moscow's military capabilities could instead trigger a nuclear response. France is pressing Germany to clarify how it would use its expanding arsenal of long-range weapons, warning that a misreading of military intentions could push the continent towards a nuclear confrontation.Paris is concerned that a conventional attack on a target deep inside Russia could be interpreted by the Kremlin as a much broader threat, particularly if Moscow believes the strike has the backing of a nuclear-armed ally. A French official told the Financial Times that a conventional weapon could hit a Russian target and still provoke a nuclear response if the signal was misunderstood.The concern has become more pressing as Germany acquires and develops ground-launched missiles with ranges of between 500 km and more than 2,000 km. The weapons would give Berlin the ability to hit military installations far inside Russian territory, a significant expansion of its conventional strike capability.France is now holding discussions with German officials to establish a common understanding of when and how such weapons could be deployed, according to six people familiar with the talks cited by the Financial Times. Paris wants Germany's approach to deep precision strikes (DPS) to be aligned with its own nuclear strategy, particularly over the risks of escalation and the messages military action could send to Moscow.The discussions expose a challenge facing Europe's rearmament drive: expanding the ability to strike an adversary is only part of deterrence; countries also need to agree on how those capabilities will be used and how to prevent an attack from being mistaken for the start of a wider war.France fears being drawn into a conflictOne source of French anxiety is president Emmanuel Macron's proposal for France to extend its nuclear deterrence discussions to other European countries. Under the concept of 'forward deterrence', Paris is exploring how its nuclear capabilities could contribute to the security of European partners, while retaining sole control over any decision to use its nuclear weapons.French officials fear that if Germany launches a deep strike against Russia, Moscow could hold France responsible for the attack because of the two countries' growing defence and deterrence cooperation.France has argued that nuclear deterrence depends not only on possessing weapons but also on a shared understanding of how threats, military movements and attacks are communicated.Paris wants a clearer doctrine, preferably one made public enough to ensure that Russia does not misinterpret the intentions behind a conventional strike.The issue is particularly relevant because France and Germany had already agreed to deepen cooperation on deterrence. In a joint declaration issued in March, Macron and German chancellor Friedrich Merz announced the creation of a high-level nuclear steering group to coordinate strategic cooperation, including conventional capabilities, missile defence and France's nuclear forces. The declaration specifically identified deep precision strikes and the management of escalation below the nuclear threshold as areas for cooperation.Germany says allies need common rulesBerlin has not rejected the French concerns. A senior German official told the Financial Times that Germany agreed European capitals needed a joint doctrine and a common understanding of the escalation ladder.The official added that the acquisition of deep-strike capabilities had always been expected to involve an agreement on how they would be deployed. Formal discussions had been delayed by France's internal debate over its nuclear strategy but were now gaining momentum.The debate also raises questions about how individual European countries would coordinate long-range attacks within Nato. Germany's growing capabilities are part of a wider effort involving Britain, Poland and Nordic and Baltic countries to strengthen Europe's ability to deter Russia, particularly as uncertainty grows over the United States' long-term security commitments under US president Donald Trump.General Ingo Gerhartz, the German officer who heads Nato's command responsible for the defence of central Europe and its eastern flank, has argued that deep-strike decisions must be taken in consultation with allies. Russia, he said at the Berlin Security Conference last week, would tend to attribute an attack by one Nato member to the alliance as a whole.Germany's defence ministry said it was developing deep precision strike capabilities jointly with Britain and exploring the possibility of including France.As countries develop weapons capable of reaching deeper into Russian territory, they must also establish how those weapons fit into a collective defence strategy, and how to ensure that a conventional operation does not become the trigger for a nuclear crisis.You use AI every day. articles.title: Scottish man confirmed as victim of Krakow shooting
articles.summary: The man, who is understood to be James Thomas Campbell from Prestwick, died when a lone gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday.
articles.body:
A 32-year-old Scottish man has been confirmed as one of the victims of a mass shooting in Poland that left six people dead.

The man, who is understood to be James Thomas Campbell from Prestwick in South Ayrshire, died when a lone gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday.

Campbell worked as a DJ in Ayrshire. Police Scotland confirmed it was providing specialist support to the victim's family, but formal identification is yet to be carried out.

The 24-year-old attacker, named as Michal Oksinski by local media, died in hospital on Monday, having also fatally shot four Polish citizens and an Austrian woman with a further 15 people, including two police officers, injured.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Det Ch Insp David McAlinden, senior investigating officer from Police Scotland's Counter Terrorism Policing unit, said the force was "aware of the tragic death of a Scottish man in Krakow".

He added: "Working in conjunction with COPFS (the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service), Police Scotland is supporting the UK counter-terrorism policing network and the Polish authorities.

"The immediate shared priority is to ensure that identification is properly established for the family, so that repatriation can take place as quickly as possible.

"The family has asked for their privacy to be respected. Our thoughts are with them and everyone impacted by this incident."

The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, a popular tourist spot.

Police said the gunman drove into the square before beginning to fire at random people from his car.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the man, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning.

In addition to the six people killed in central Krakow, police later found the bodies of the gunman's parents and sister at his address on Saturday.

Earlier this week two friends from Aberdeen described how they ran for their lives as the shooting started .

Ciaran McMenemy, 26, and Charlie Hutchison, 27, said they had just sat down for a drink when the gunfire began. They quickly fled and took shelter.

articles.title: ‘No deliberate action to unbalance election’: Brazil’s top electoral court fines Meta for non-compliance
articles.summary: In a unanimous ruling, Brazil's top electoral court found no preliminary evidence that US tech giant Meta had deliberately acted to influence the outcome
articles.body: In a unanimous ruling, Brazil's top electoral court found no preliminary evidence that US tech giant Meta had deliberately acted to influence the outcome of last month's presidential election runoff, but fined its Facebook platform 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million) for failing to fully comply with judicial orders."The records contain technical failures acknowledged by Facebook itself, but there are no elements allowing us to conclude, on a preliminary basis, that there was deliberate action to unbalance the election," Justice Marco Aurelio Bellizze wrote in the ruling, referring to submissions made by Meta."That conclusion would require robust evidence, to be produced through the appropriate legal proceedings," he added.The coalition led by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who secured re-election, had filed a complaint ahead of last month's vote, alleging restrictions on the distribution of its posts, the activity of purportedly inauthentic accounts, failures to identify AI-generated content and disparities in the functioning of Meta's tools that allegedly favoured right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.Bolsonaro lost the runoff despite securing more votes than Lula in the first round. He has since fled to the US with his family.Meta informed the court last month that it had adopted measures to ensure equal treatment of the two campaigns."Meta complies with Brazilian electoral law and applies the same rules to all candidates and parties. We will continue to present the facts and defend ourselves against false allegations in the ongoing legal proceedings," the Mark Zuckerberg-led company maintained in a statement on Wednesday.However, the court found that Meta had either failed to comply with certain directives, only partially fulfilled them or acted after the stipulated deadlines.According to Justice Bellizze, the fine reflected the company's overall conduct in responding to the court's orders, including delays, incomplete information and difficulties in verifying some of the data submitted.The penalty comprises three daily fines of 500,000 reais between October 17 and 19, followed by six daily fines of 1 million reais between October 20 and 25.Lula has long pledged to tighten regulations governing social media in Brazil. In his victory speech, he declared: "We had to overcome foreign interference in the election, coming from outside through digital platforms that we will have to regulate."(With Reuters inputs)You use AI every day.
